bindings.role: withRecordSnapshot supplies checked state to primary readers; executeRecordStore serves advanced inspect/check/record/recover; executeTargetedStore invokes construction and receipt preparation within the selected preview or execution path.
constructMutation realizes the pure candidate-construction part of prepare_record_candidate.
primaryReceiptPreparer receives guarded candidate/storage facts and returns the prepared command-owned receipt.
inspectSubjects and its RecordFiles reader realize the declared-subject observation part; the logical operation does not have a dedicated exported function with the same name.

mechanism: Direct in-process JavaScript calls and callbacks, without a network endpoint or serialized RPC boundary. Logical operation names are not asserted to be exported symbols.
addressing: The caller supplies root and change_id or declared subject paths. The Module-owned filesystem addressing is recorded in MOD-011; no new public service address is defined here.
failure_compatibility: The engine reports or throws typed store failures for the command adapters to map into their own envelopes. Advanced Store.record revalidates candidate and before-state after acquiring exclusion; targeted execution constructs under exclusion. Preview uses the snapshot path without acquiring a writer lock.

Receipt preparation precedes journal creation/replacement for changed publication; recovery prepares from verified retained state, and a committed journal rejects restore. This source observation does not establish executed satisfaction of all logical failure outcomes.

sources.basis: Static source inspection records conditional operation order, terminal alternatives, coordination guards, and exact recovery boundaries under the current CLI/Records contracts. No product operation, failure injection, transaction recovery, platform test, or requirement verification was executed; source order is not inferred from Scenario traceability.

sequences.name: Record publication
preconditions: The caller selects a root and change, supplies an explicit supported v3 targeted mutation, expected revision, and declared decision-basis identities. The main sequence describes a changed targeted write; the preview and unchanged cases terminate separately.

The current CLI and Records contracts govern admission, complete candidate structure, preservation, and storage-only results. Source observations do not authorize a write or supply an engineering decision.

steps.name: Admit explicit request
steps.action: The mutation adapter validates request transport and selectors, then calls executeTargetedStore with construction and receipt-preparation callbacks. It does not infer missing decisions.

steps.name: Inspect preview snapshot
steps.action: Use the gated coherent snapshot path without acquiring the writer lock; construct the candidate from explicit intent and validate structure, preservation, expected revision, target identities, and declared read basis.

steps.name: Prepare preview receipt
steps.action: The bounded receipt callback serializes valid with both inspected before revision and candidate revision; candidate changed targets and observations are not saved effects.

steps.name: Recheck preview coherence
steps.action: The snapshot wrapper repeats gate/epoch and record revision checks before returning the prepared preview. It creates no reservation, journal, or transaction lock/epoch.

branches.outcome: Return valid preview with no authoritative or private transaction writes. Actual execution must repeat freshness checks; preview does not reserve a later save.

steps.name: Inspect coherent before-state
steps.action: Read the selected registered v3 record set through snapshot. Reader gates reject a live writer or retained transaction attention; gate/epoch and record revision checks exclude a mixed snapshot presented as usable.

steps.name: Acquire writer exclusion
steps.action: Create the private directory when necessary, exclusively create the writer lock with an ownership token, and update the epoch. Competing CLI writers are excluded; these private effects precede authoritative publication.

steps.name: Construct and recheck candidate
steps.action: Require no retained journal, reread the before-set under exclusion, compare its revision with the initial snapshot, construct the lossless complete candidate, and validate the expected revision, target identities, declared reads, references, and preservation rules. No declared identity is silently refreshed.

steps.name: Prepare bounded receipt
steps.action: Store.record determines whether candidate bytes changed and invokes the command-owned primary receipt callback before journal creation or target replacement. Serialize the storage result and bounded diagnostic summary; optional details may be explicitly omitted. A prepared saved receipt remains private until commit succeeds.

branches.condition: The fresh complete candidate has exactly the before revision.

steps.name: Release unchanged writer
steps.action: Release the owned lock and return the already prepared unchanged receipt. Do not create a journal or replace authoritative files; lock/epoch setup may already have occurred.

branches.outcome: Return unchanged with an empty changed list and exact authoritative before bytes. This fresh no-op is not a replay facility for a stale request.

steps.name: Persist prepared journal
steps.action: Retain exact before and candidate bytes/identities, declared writes and reads, transaction identity, and created-directory tracking in a phase=prepared journal under owned exclusion. Retention precedes authoritative replacement.

steps.name: Publish exact candidate bytes
steps.action: Recheck declared read identities, recognize every target as its recorded before or candidate value, and publish only declared candidate writes through guarded filesystem operations. Repeat ownership, known-state, and target checks during replacement; verify all candidate identities afterward.

steps.name: Persist committed phase
steps.action: Recheck the declared read basis after replacement and before commitment, then durably rewrite the journal with phase=committed. Failures do not expose the prepared saved receipt as successful publication.

steps.name: Clean up and return receipt
steps.action: After commitment, remove the exact retained journal, release owned exclusion, and return the previously prepared receipt for command output. Cleanup failure remains transaction attention; it is not an authorized rollback of committed content.

sequences.outcome: The successfully completed source path returns saved for the exact candidate and a storage-only claim after commit and cleanup. Output delivery remains a separate transport boundary.

failures.condition: Admission, coherent inspection, freshness, candidate validation, or receipt preparation fails before a journal/authoritative replacement.
failures.outcome: Return the applicable rejected, conflict, busy, or recovery-required result; do not publish the candidate.
effects: Authoritative records are not changed by this failed attempt before publication. After non-preview exclusion begins, private directories, epoch, or lock cleanup effects may already exist.
Unavailable or malformed state is not converted into an empty current snapshot or a successful no-op.

failures.condition: A non-crash failure occurs after the prepared journal is created but before committed phase.
failures.outcome: The source attempts guarded restoration of exact before bytes and cleanup. If that succeeds, report the original failure; otherwise require explicit recovery.
effects: Restoration checks every current target against retained before/candidate identities and removes only tracked transaction-created files or empty created directories where permitted.
Observed unknown target bytes, missing/tampered evidence, or failed restoration prevent guessed repair; recovery metadata is reported only when available.

failures.condition: Execution is interrupted, commitment/cleanup is uncertain, or a failure occurs with a committed journal.
failures.outcome: Report recovery-required when control returns with transaction attention, or leave the interrupted caller without a success receipt. Do not claim rollback or saved content from an unknown outcome.
effects: Readers do not expose an unfinished mixed store as current. Exact retained state and explicit recovery selection govern subsequent work.
A lost stdout response after successful commitment is a transport/lost-response problem. Retrying the old expected revision does not authorize replay; reread and reassess.

constraints: This ordered account is derived from executeTargetedStore, Store.record, and the primary receipt callback. It is not inferred from SCN-046 participation. The advanced record path uses the same publisher but validates its supplied complete candidate before and after acquiring exclusion instead of using targeted construction.
Receipt preparation precedes private journal creation and authoritative replacement; it does not turn a future saved result into an observed success.

CLI exclusion coordinates participating writers. External editors are covered only at observed identity checks; an exact-target edit after the final check may still be overwritten under the retained contract.
Calls execute synchronously inside the existing CLI process. Source inspection supplies no durability, crash, output-transport, concurrency, platform, or requirement-satisfaction evidence.

sequences.name: Record recovery
preconditions: The caller explicitly selects the root/change, exact transaction ID, current expected recovery digest, and complete or restore action. Recovery does not construct a new decision or candidate.

The retained journal must be supported v3, canonical and internally consistent, with verified exact before/candidate snapshots and declared scope. A missing, tampered, stale, or unrecognized journal is not repair authority.

steps.name: Admit explicit recovery
steps.action: Validate selectors and the closed complete/restore action before dispatching the exact recovery request to executeRecordStore.

steps.name: Validate retained journal
steps.action: Before exclusion, load the expected journal bytes and verify their digest, transaction/change identity, canonical encoding, supported version and prepared/committed phase, snapshot content hashes, scope, preservation, write/read sets, and tracked directory identities.

steps.name: Acquire recovery exclusion
steps.action: Reject a live competing lock owner. Remove an exactly observed stale owner lock when admitted, exclusively acquire a new owned lock, and update the epoch. Private coordination effects are distinct from authoritative recovery.

steps.name: Recheck recovery admissibility
steps.action: Reload the exact expected journal under exclusion and require every observed target to equal its retained before or candidate identity, including absence. A committed journal requires candidate identities and rejects restore; it cannot authorize rollback.

branches.condition: The requested action is restore and the verified journal is prepared.

steps.name: Prepare before-state recovery receipt
steps.action: Prepare and validate the recovered result against the exact retained before-set before touching authoritative files. Restoration does not require external read-basis files to retain their old values and never writes those files.

steps.name: Restore exact retained before bytes
steps.action: Publish the retained before-set with repeated exclusion, containment, and known-state checks. Remove only permitted transaction-created files and tracked empty directories; do not overwrite an observed third state or unrelated content.

steps.name: Finish verified restoration
steps.action: Verify the terminal before identities, remove the retained journal, release owned exclusion, and return the prepared recovered receipt. Failure at any point preserves an explicit incomplete/unknown outcome for reinspection.

branches.outcome: Return recovered for the verified exact before-state only after successful restoration and cleanup. No workflow decision, replay, or blanket project rollback is performed.

steps.name: Prepare candidate recovery receipt
steps.action: For complete, verify the retained declared read basis and prepare/validate a recovered result against the exact retained candidate before authoritative writes. The advanced recovery result is prepared within Store.prepareResult.

steps.name: Complete exact retained candidate
steps.action: Publish the retained candidate with repeated owned-lock, path, target before/candidate, and decision-basis checks. A committed journal permits only candidate bytes; unknown values stop completion.

steps.name: Recheck basis and commit recovery
steps.action: Recheck declared reads after candidate publication. For a prepared journal, observed basis drift attempts guarded restoration before reporting failure. Otherwise persist phase=committed; a previously committed journal is never rolled back.

steps.name: Finish verified completion
steps.action: Remove the verified terminal journal, release the owned lock, and return the prepared recovered result. Interrupted cleanup or a subsequent failure requires reinspection with the current recovery identity.

sequences.outcome: Return recovered for the exact retained candidate after verified completion and cleanup. The result proves no new engineering decision, requirement satisfaction, or successful output delivery.

failures.condition: A selected journal, snapshot, target, action, version, or identity is missing, changed, incompatible, or untrusted; a target matches neither retained side.
failures.outcome: Stop recovery without guessing state or replaying actor intent. The advanced wrapper reports recovery-required, except a live writer is busy.
effects: Checks made before exclusion produce no recovery writes; later rejection may follow private lock/epoch effects. Missing recovery metadata is reported as unavailable, not invented.
A committed journal with an observed before-state target is inconsistent and rejected. Restore is rejected even when a committed journal otherwise validates.

failures.condition: Completion observes changed declared read basis, or a restore/complete filesystem operation or cleanup is interrupted.
failures.outcome: Keep the actual incomplete or uncertain recovery outcome explicit; reinspection and an explicitly selected current recovery identity are required.
effects: Before committed phase, the source may attempt exact guarded restoration after post-publication basis drift. That attempt is not a guarantee that all previous bytes were restored.
After committed phase, no recovery path restores before bytes. Retained evidence and known target identities govern completion/cleanup, not a blind retry.

constraints: Main steps describe complete; the restore branch is terminal and does not rejoin candidate completion. Every branch/failure remains conditional on its stated source checks.
Repeated recovery must use the current retained transaction identity/digest and cannot synthesize a replacement transaction. Recovery may itself be interrupted.

The same observed-check external-edit boundary applies to complete and restore. Source code inspection does not establish all-platform atomicity, durability, crash recovery, or consumer-visible verification.

proposed.choice: Realize this logical contract through the existing in-process store calls and bounded construction/receipt callbacks.
proposed.rationale: The co-located Modules need checked candidate context and strict sequencing, not an independent remote transport.
alternatives: A serialized IPC or network protocol would require a new identity, failure, retry, and receipt-readiness protocol.
consequences: Preserve store control of candidate freshness and publication. Callbacks must not grant pure construction write authority or let presentation reinterpret a committed result.
revisit_when: Persistence moves into another process or trust boundary, requiring a new physical binding with equivalent logical guarantees.

deferred: The mapping is not a new public JavaScript API or a source-level conformance claim. Operation-level verification and any extraction of shared helpers remain separate implementation work.
